===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:plante<ety:inh<ang:plante>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|plante}}, from {{inh|en|ang|plante||young tree or shrub, herb newly planted}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*plantu}}, from {{der|en|la|planta||sprout, shoot, cutting}}. Broader sense of "any vegetable life, vegetation generally" is from {{cog|fro|plante}}. {{doublet|en|clan}} (borrowed through Celtic languages) and {{doublet|en|planta|notext=1}} (directly from Latin).

The verb is from {{inh|en|enm|planten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|plantian|t=to plant}}, from {{der|en|la|plantō|plantāre}}, later influenced by {{cog|fro|planter}}. Compare also {{cog|nl|planten||to plant}}, {{cog|de|pflanzen||to plant}}, {{cog|sv|plantera||to plant}}, {{cog|is|planta||to plant}}.

The ''factory'' and ''machinery'' senses comes from the Latin sense of "any vegetable production that serves to propagate the species," which refers to something that produces.

====Usage notes====
* The scientific criteria for classifying organisms as plants underwent significant revision during the twentieth century. As a result, groups such as bacteria, algae, and fungi are no longer included within the plant kingdom by specialists in their respective fields. Despite these advances, many textbooks have yet to incorporate the most current perspectives on biological classification.
